text: Insight [in + sight]: Ger. Einsicht , Anschauung ; Fr. connaissance profonde (no exact equivalent); Ital. intuizione . (1) Apprehension of the more subtle and profound aspects of truth in a relatively immediate and direct way. (2) The organ of higher intuition or reason, held to afford direct contemplation of truth. The use of the term varies from the more refined and penetrating processes of thought to the supposed faculty of CONTEMPLATION (q.v.) of the mystics. ( J.M.B. )
